attackClasses.i_knownAnswer: the papers' own worked examples (Bailey & López de Prado publish DSR/PSR; the CSCV construction) recomputed through the frozen rigor — a mismatch is a candidate break. attackClasses.ii_property: monotonicity (DSR falls as trials rise; PSR→0 as the benchmark rises; PBO invariant to column order), symmetry, scale-invariance where theory demands it
attackClasses.iii_degenerate: constant series, single observation, T shorter than the moment window, all-identical columns, NaN/Inf propagation, zero variance
attackClasses.iv_adversarial: extreme skew/kurtosis at float boundaries, autocorrelated series (the i.i.d. assumption probed deliberately), ties in CSCV ranking, N=1, odd S

dd49_mathRedTeam.threeWayClassification: every finding classified into EXACTLY ONE of: BREAK (the code contradicts its own paper) · ASSUMPTION-LIMIT (the code is faithful; the input violates an assumption the paper states — i.i.d., moments exist — and the code should refuse or flag rather than emit) · THEORY-GAP (the paper itself is ambiguous; both readings shown). A BREAK misclassified as assumption-limit is a cover-up; an assumption-limit misclassified as BREAK is slander of the frozen core. The classification is the red team's hardest task and it is walled (S136).
